# Engine source patches

The QuickJS-NG engine source under `vendor/quickjs/source_ng` is a git submodule
pinned to an upstream commit. Our hand-written NativeScript changes are kept here
as a patch applied on top of that pristine checkout, rather than baked into a
vendored copy. The engine source is shared by the Apple and Android builds, which
is why both the source and its patches live under `vendor/` rather than under
`platforms/<platform>/`.

```
vendor/quickjs/
  source_ng/                                          (submodule, pristine upstream)
  patches/source_ng/0001-nativescript-local-changes.patch
```

QuickJS-NG is the only QuickJS lane left: the bellard tree was dropped, and
`QUICKJS` is an alias for `QUICKJS_NG` (see `test-app/runtime/build.gradle`).

The patch touches `quickjs.c` / `quickjs.h` only: the `USE_HOST_OBJECT`
host-object hooks in `JS_GetPropertyInternal` (host objects act as a non-masking
prototype fallback), the weak-ref keep-alive pair
(`JS_KeepWeakRefTargetAlive` / `JS_ClearWeakRefKeepAlives`, required by
`vendor/quickjs/quickjs-api.c`), `JS_EVAL_FLAG_COMPILE_ONLY_NO_RESOLVE` (required
by the Apple `node:vm` module), and the functions after the `/* CUSTOM */`
marker.

## Managing them

The patch is generated by diffing the working tree against the pinned commit:

```
git -C vendor/quickjs/source_ng diff > vendor/quickjs/patches/source_ng/0001-nativescript-local-changes.patch
```

Because the submodule work tree is patched in place it is always dirty, which is
expected -- `.gitmodules` sets `ignore = dirty` so `git status` stays quiet. Edit
the engine by editing that work tree, then regenerate the patch with the command
above.

On a fresh checkout / in CI, fetch the submodule first, then patch it:

```
git submodule update --init --force vendor/quickjs/source_ng
npm run patch-quickjs      # = node scripts/apply_quickjs_patches.js
```

Fetching is a deliberate manual step, so no script can move you off the pin
behind your back. The patch script hard-resets the submodule work tree to the
pinned commit and re-applies the patch, so it is idempotent; `--check` verifies
the patch still applies (in a throwaway worktree) without touching anything.

Never pass `--remote` to `git submodule update`: that moves the submodule to the
tip of its branch and off the pin, silently changing the engine and its
`BC_VERSION`.

## Compatibility

The submodule commit sets the engine's `BC_VERSION`. The compile-time bytecode
CLI (see `.github/workflows/bytecode-compilers.yml`) MUST be built from the same
commit, or `JS_ReadObject` rejects the produced bytecode at runtime. The app then
dies on launch with no JS error at all -- on Android it surfaces as
`Failed to create JavaScript extend wrapper for class 'com/tns/NativeScriptActivity'`,
because no module ever loaded. Keep the workflow ref and the submodule pin in
lock-step.

To check what a built APK actually shipped, the byte right after the 12-byte
container header is the engine's `BC_VERSION`:

```
unzip -p app-release.apk assets/app/bundle.js | head -c 16 | xxd
grep -m1 'define BC_VERSION' vendor/quickjs/source_ng/quickjs.c
```

Current pin: `d950d55e950dd7994a96c669c31efa967b8b79f3` (`BC_VERSION 27`).
